title: Sequential migrateOut batch exits through AMM-backed strategy distribute non-uniform haircuts across identical-principal users
description: When a token's principal is routed through an AMM-backed strategy (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy, which sells vault shares via a Curve pool on withdrawal) and the pool is underwater (negative yield), migrateOut enters the payout<totalPrincipal scaling branch (line 341) that distributes the realized payout pro-rata across the batch's principal. Because a multi-batch migration performs one _routeExit AMM sell per batch (line 334), each successive sell walks the AMM price down, so each batch realizes a different effective price. The per-batch haircut ratio (payout/totalPrincipal) is computed over only that batch's principal, so two users with identical principal in different batches are credited materially different amounts. Earlier-batch users receive a smaller haircut; later-batch users subsidize them. The M-01 fix's stated 'pro-rata distribution' intent is therefore not achieved uniformly across the full migration.
impact: Cross-user value redistribution of principal. Two users with identical principal in different migrateOut batches receive materially different realized amounts (e.g. ~960 vs ~940 on 1000 principal). No value leaves the protocol; Sigma amounts <= payout (conservation holds), so this is a value leak between users, not theft or protocol loss.
attackPath: 1. A token's principal is routed through ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy (sells vault shares via a Curve AMM on withdrawal).
2. The strategy is underwater / below par (negative yield), so migrateOut's payout < totalPrincipal scaling branch (line 341) activates.
3. Migrator performs migrateOut across multiple sequential batches (each batch is one _routeExit AMM sell at line 334).
4. Earlier AMM sells realize a higher effective price (smaller per-batch haircut); each later sell walks the AMM price down (larger haircut).
5. Each batch computes its haircut ratio as payout/totalPrincipal over ONLY that batch's principal, so identical-principal users in different batches are credited unequally.
recommendation: Compute the haircut ratio over the full migration's aggregate realized payout and aggregate principal (single uniform ratio applied to all users), or settle all AMM sells first and distribute pro-rata against the combined proceeds, so that identical-principal users receive identical haircuts regardless of batch ordering.
